q: How do I calculate the carbon footprint of machine embroidery?
title: Machine embroidery carbon footprint
short: Read the embroidery unit's electricity for a period, multiply by the grid factor and divide by metres or pieces embroidered. Add thread, backing and sequins by weight. Machines run on electricity, so the bill is most of the unit's own figure.
audience: Embroidery units, including Surat multi-head machine owners

ul: Multi-head embroidery machines, usually the largest load.
Lighting, fans and air conditioning in the machine hall.
Cutting and finishing tables, and steam irons.
Viscose, polyester or zari thread by weight.
The base fabric, if your figure covers it.

p: Stitch count drives machine time. Report per metre for running embroidery and per piece for panels, with the stitch count.

example.title: Worked example: embroidery unit per metre (one month)
lines: Plant total: 14,200 / 100,000 = 0.142 kg CO2 per metre
Add thread, backing and base fabric for the full figure
example.note: Inputs are illustrative; use your own bills and production records.

senseible: Senseible reads the plant's electricity bills (CEA grid factor 0.710 kg CO2 per kWh, CO2 Baseline Database version 21.0) and fuel invoices (IPCC 2006 defaults) into a fingerprinted Scope 1 and 2 record, the plant-level input to a per-unit figure. Bought-in materials go to the supplier evidence trail; product reports are self-declared drafts.
